metadata.title: When is a polynomial in three variables cylindrical?
metadata.abstract: We prove that a nonconstant polynomial $f\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,x_2,x_3]$ is cylindrical (that is, $f\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,x_2]$ after an invertible linear change of coordinates) if and only if its bordered Hessian determinant vanishes identically. The same conclusion holds over $\mathbb{R}$. We also give explicit counterexamples to this criterion in every dimension $n\ge4$.

metadata.title: Inscribed 4-polytopes of maximal volume with seven and eight vertices
metadata.abstract: We prove, with sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, that every cyclic $4$-polytope with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $2/5$. Hence no $4$-polytope of maximal volume with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ is cyclic, answering a question of Horváth and Lángi for $d = 4$, and with their theorem the maximal volume is $\sqrt{3}/4$. With eight vertices, the same method bounds the volume of every simplicial type other than the cross-polytope by $13/20$, so the regular cross-polytope, of volume $2/3$, is up to orthogonal transformations the unique maximiser.

metadata.title: Disc-presheaves and normal invariants
metadata.abstract: In this note, we elaborate on a result of Krannich--Kupers--Mehzer on Disc-presheaves. metadata.title: The Volume Exchange Metric
metadata.abstract: The volume exchange metric between cell structures embedded in Euclidean space is introduced. Intuitively, it measures the minimum amount of volume that must be swept out to continuously transform one cell structure into another. The main result is that the volume exchange metric coincides with a discrete analogue defined as a minimum over matchings between cells. Algorithms are described to compute the discrete volume exchange metric and illustrate its effectiveness at distinguishing polycrystalline microstructures in computational experiments.

metadata.title: Flux Vacua, Asymptotic Periods, and Relatively Anosov Representations
metadata.abstract: We develop a topological method to detect classical flux vacua of M-theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds with a single complex structure modulus using only asymptotic period data and monodromy information. To this end, we express the index of the F-term of the flux superpotential as a winding number along the boundary of the universal cover of the complex structure moduli space. The index evaluates to a sum over zeros and poles of a suitably normalized boundary F-term, where local contributions can be computed algebraically on a dense set of boundary points. Assuming a conjectured bound on the remaining contributions, sufficiently many sign changes of the boundary F-term guarantee a flux vacuum in the interior. We illustrate the method on the mirror Fermat sextic with explicit examples and a systematic flux scan. A main technical ingredient in our construction is a continuity result for projective period maps: we prove that the non-holomorphic (3,1)-period map extends continuously to the boundary of the covering space if the monodromy representation is relatively Anosov. In general, this property does not hold for holomorphic (4,0)-periods.

metadata.title: Tree Lattices and the Neumann-Zagier conjecture
metadata.abstract: A tree with integer weights on its vertices presents an integral lattice called a tree lattice. We prove that if a tree lattice is positive definite, then one of the vertex elements is irreducible, i.e. determines a facet of its Voronoi polyhedron. As a corollary, we settle a 1985 conjecture of Neumann and Zagier: if a tree lattice is isometric to the lattice of integer points in Euclidean space, then the tree contains a vertex of weight one.

metadata.title: Orthogonal group sections via light bulb systems
metadata.abstract: For any oriented, smooth $4$--manifold $X$ diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times S^2)^{\# n}\# D^4$, this paper shows that the natural group homomorphism $$\mathrm{Mod}(X,\partial X)\to \mathrm{O}(H_2(X;\mathbb{Z}))$$ admits a section. In fact, every light bulb system in $X$ gives rise to a section, which can be characterized uniquely in terms of implanted barbell twists and implanted crossbell involutions. Moreover, all sections arising from different light bulb systems become identical after a single $S^2\times S^2$--stabilization of $X$.

metadata.title: Geometry of a class of $φ$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2\times \mathbb{R}$
metadata.abstract: We study a class of $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in the product space $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$, that is, weighted minimal surfaces whose corresponding weight is determined by a smooth potential function $\varphi$ that depends only on the height coordinate relative to the factor $\mathbb{R}$. Under monotonicity, concavity, and asymptotic conditions on $\varphi$, we obtain a complete classification of connected, properly embedded $\varphi$-minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$ acting trivially on $\mathbb{R}$ and by rotations or parabolic translations on $\mathbb{H}^2$. Finally, we establish several non-existence results for $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{R}$, either by using properties of the height function or by applying the tangency principle together with suitable invariant surfaces as barriers.

metadata.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
metadata.abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

analysisBasis.abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. metadata.title: $L^{p}$-parabolicity of Riemannian manifolds
metadata.abstract: We describe the $L^p$-parabolicity of a Riemannian manifold in terms of a unified theory of nonlinear $L^p$-capacities, for the whole range $1\leq p\leq \infty$. For example, the \(L^{1}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to the usual notion of parabolicity/recurrence, while \(L^{2}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to biparabolicity. For any $1\leq p\leq \infty,$ the $L^p$-parabolicity turns out to be equivalent to the $L^q$-Liouville property for positive superharmonic functions, where $p$ and $q$ are Hölder conjugate exponents. We also provide a new capacitary characterization of the $L^1$-Liouville property. Finally we obtain an almost optimal volume growth condition for the $L^p$-parabolicity for $1<p\leq 2$ as well as a sharp volume condition for all $1<p<\infty$ for manifolds of non-negative Ricci curvature and for model manifolds.

metadata.title: Weak reducibility for bridge trisections
metadata.abstract: A bridge splitting of a knot is weakly reducible if it has a pair of disjoint shadows, one from above and one from below, in the splitting surface. The process of weak reduction exchanges local minima and maxima in the splitting, untelescoping the splitting and giving a method for detecting essential surfaces in the knot complement. We define weak reducibility in this context, giving diagrammatic conditions for carrying out a weak reduction operation on bridge splittings. We produce a partial classification of 4-bridge trisections of surfaces in $S^4$.

metadata.title: Triviality of $K$-homology classes of Euler characteristic operators of stratified pseudomanifolds
metadata.abstract: We show that the $K$-homology classes of the Euler characteristic operators associated with the minimal and maximal ideal boundary conditions of the de Rham differential on the regular part of a connected compact Thom-Mather stratified pseudomanifold, equipped with an adapted metric, are trivial beyond their indices. metadata.title: Rotations, Shears, and Two-Generation on Spheres
metadata.abstract: For every round sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, we exhibit two explicit divergence-free vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. One generator is an elementary planar rotation, \[ A=R_{12}, \] while the other combines a linearly modulated planar rotation with a chain of adjacent planar rotations: \[ B=x_3R_{12}+\sum_{k=2}^n R_{k,k+1}. \] Thus two one-parameter groups suffice, and two is the smallest possible number. The proof separates naturally into two steps. We first show that the $n$ adjacent rotations \[ R_{12},R_{23},\ldots,R_{n,n+1} \] together with the shear $x_3R_{12}$ generate, through their flows, a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. The infinitesimal argument is organized by transverse vector spherical harmonics. For $n\ge4$ the relevant harmonic spaces are irreducible $SO(n+1)$-modules; on $S^2$ the argument reduces to the Hamiltonian/Poisson formalism; and on $S^3$ the transverse harmonic spaces split into two curl eigenspaces. We then show that all $n+1$ of these vector fields lie in the Lie algebra generated by $A$ and $B$. A Casimir operator separates the quadratic shear from the linear rotational terms, after which the remaining rotations can be recovered successively. Finally, standard approximation formulas for flows convert the Lie-algebraic generation result into $C^\infty$ density in $\SDiff_0(S^n)$.

metadata.title: An orthogonality inequality in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$ and the double-cap conjecture
metadata.abstract: The orthogonal neighborhood of a set in real projective space is the union of the hyperplanes perpendicular to its points. We prove that caps minimize neighborhood measure among measurable sets of fixed measure in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$, for $n \geq 3$, with rigidity up to null sets. This yields the double-cap conjecture: a measurable subset of $S^{n-1}$ containing no orthogonal pair has measure at most that of two opposite open caps of radius $\pi/4$. The argument combines compactness of the Funk transform, rotation comparisons, and projective variations. We also obtain qualitative stability and determine the measurable fractional chromatic number of the spherical orthogonality graph. AI played an assistive role in preparing this paper. The formalization and verification workflow for a separate Lean 4 proof of the main inequality and double-cap result, based on a different argument, were carried out almost entirely using AI-assisted tools.

metadata.title: A cut-and-project set which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice
metadata.abstract: We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. This answers a question of Burago and Kleiner about cut-and-project sets, and shows in particular that the hypothesis of boundary measure zero is not enough to guarantee bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice. Since our set has uniform density, it also shows that a non-rectifiable Delone set need not encode a non-realisable density, answering a question of Bhat and Dymond.

metadata.title: Multiplicity of closed geodesics on odd-dimensional bumpy Finsler compact space form
metadata.abstract: Let $M = S^{2n+1}/\Gamma$ be a manifold diffeomorphic to a compact space form, endowed with a bumpy Finsler metric $F$. In this paper, we prove that there exist at least $n+3$ contractible minimal closed geodesics on $M$, assuming that all contractible minimal closed geodesics have non-zero Morse indices. Here, a contractible closed geodesic is called minimal if it is not an iteration of any other contractible closed geodesic. In particular, this confirms the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture for the bumpy quotient manifold $(S^3/\Gamma, F)$ under the non-zero Morse index assumption.

metadata.abstract: We determine the maximum ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems. metadata.title: Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups
metadata.abstract: We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups $C_W$ associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems $(W,S)$. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of $C_{W_T}$ for some spherical subset $T\subseteq S$. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types $B$, $D$, $E$, $F$, and $H$, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine $C_{W(I_2(p))}$ directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When $S$ is finite, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups of $C_W$. In type $A$, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group $J_n$ if and only if it embeds into a Sylow $2$-subgroup of the symmetric group $S_n$. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types $A$ and $B$ and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.

metadata.title: Sharp boundedness criteria for nonnegative kernels on regular curves in the Heisenberg group
metadata.abstract: In this paper we study singular integrals associated with the nonnegative kernels \[ K_\alpha(x,y,z)=\frac{|z|^{\alpha/2}}{\|(x,y,z)\|^{\alpha+1}}, \qquad \alpha>0, \] in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb H$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Korányi norm. This family was introduced by Chousionis and Li. We first show that there exists a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve $E\subset\mathbb H$ such that the singular integrals associated with $K_\alpha$ are unbounded on $L^2(E)$ for every $0<\alpha<4$. This extends the counterexamples of Chousionis, Li and Zhang from $0<\alpha<2$ to the full range $0<\alpha<4$. Combined with the boundedness theorem of Fässler and Orponen for $\alpha\ge4$, our result determines the exact range of exponents for boundedness on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve. We also consider the more general kernels \[ K_\Phi(p)=\frac{1}{\|p\|} \Phi\!\left(\frac{|z|^{1/2}}{\|p\|}\right), \qquad p=(x,y,z)\neq0, \] where $\Phi:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and nondecreasing, with $\Phi(0)=0$. We show that the associated singular integral is $L^2$-bounded on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve if and only if $\Phi(u)=O(u^4)$ as $u\to0$. When this condition fails, we construct a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve on which the operator is unbounded. The curves in both constructions can be chosen as horizontal lifts of planar $C^1$ graphs with arbitrarily small slope.

metadata.title: Eliminating the Higgs field and perturbing Yang-Mills connections in cone Yang-Mills theory
metadata.abstract: We study the configurations of the cone Yang-Mills functional over a closed connected manifold. We show that the Euler-Lagrange equation from variations in the Higgs field is always uniquely solvable for $\zeta \neq 0$, allowing us to eliminate one of the two equations from the theory. By eliminating the equation, we obtain a family of ``effective cone Yang-Mills functionals'' on the space of connection 1-forms indexed by $\zeta$, which reduce to Yang-Mills theory when $\zeta = 0$. This suggests a way to nontrivially deform the Yang-Mills moduli space. We take the first step towards this deformation by showing that, near certain critical points of the Yang-Mills functional, there is a family of smooth connections $A_t$ which satisfy the $t\zeta$-cone Yang-Mills equations.

metadata.title: Metrization of the Fell Topology and the Wijsman Topology for the Box Metric on Closed Downward Families
metadata.abstract: We study nonempty Box-closed families of metric measure spaces that are downward under the Lipschitz order. If a space is below a member in this order, it also belongs to the family. Such families need not be pyramids, because directedness is an additional condition. We define a metric on these families by taking the supremum, over all finite metric measure spaces, of the normalized absolute difference between the infimal Box distances from each finite space to the two families. We divide each difference by the sum of the support cardinality and diameter of the finite test space. The topology induced by this metric agrees on the full domain with the relative Fell topology and with the restriction of the Wijsman topology for the Box metric. On the subspace of pyramids, it induces the weak topology and makes the natural inclusion into the hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets a topological embedding for either hyperspace topology. Pyramids associated with metric measure spaces are dense in the pyramid space, which is the completion of metric measure spaces under the metric pulled back along the map that sends each space to its associated pyramid.

metadata.title: Almgren minimality of products of simplex-skeleton cones
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every $m,n\geq 2$, the orthogonal product $S_m\times S_n\subset\R^m\times\R^n$ is an Almgren minimal cone of dimension $m+n-2$, where $S_k\subset\R^k$ is the cone over the $(k-2)$-skeleton of a regular $k$-simplex. Lawlor and Morgan \cite{LM94} proved the minimality of each $S_k$ by paired calibrations, while Guy David \cite{DJT, GD13} later raised the general question whether products of Almgren minimal sets remain minimal. Our theorem gives a affirmative answer to this product question within the entire Lawlor-Morgan regular-simplex family. It extends the isolated example \(\Y\times \Y\), the product of two 1-dimensional $\Y$ sets, proved in 2014 by the second author, simultaneously to all pairwise products \(S_m\times S_n\), and therefore produces a large new family of possible codimension-two singularities for Plateau's problem. The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.

analysisBasis.abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every $m,n\geq 2$, the orthogonal product $S_m\times S_n\subset\R^m\times\R^n$ is an Almgren minimal cone of dimension $m+n-2$, where $S_k\subset\R^k$ is the cone over the $(k-2)$-skeleton of a regular $k$-simplex. Lawlor and Morgan \cite{LM94} proved the minimality of each $S_k$ by paired calibrations, while Guy David \cite{DJT, GD13} later raised the general question whether products of Almgren minimal sets remain minimal. Our theorem gives a affirmative answer to this product question within the entire Lawlor-Morgan regular-simplex family. It extends the isolated example \(\Y\times \Y\), the product of two 1-dimensional $\Y$ sets, proved in 2014 by the second author, simultaneously to all pairwise products \(S_m\times S_n\), and therefore produces a large new family of possible codimension-two singularities for Plateau's problem. The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.

metadata.title: Solid-angle formulas for simplicial cones and random shifted sections of polytopes
metadata.abstract: We consider simplicial cones $C = \operatorname{pos}(v_1, \ldots, v_n) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose generators have a Gram matrix of the form $(\langle v_i, v_j \rangle)_{i,j=1}^n = \operatorname{Id}_n+\sum_{j=1}^p \lambda_j u_j u_j^T$, where $p\in \{0,\ldots, n\}$, $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_p > -1$ and $u_1,\ldots, u_p \in \mathbb{R}^n$ are orthogonal unit vectors. We derive an explicit $p$-dimensional integral formula for the solid angle of $C$ involving the analytic continuation of the standard normal distribution function. As an application, explicit formulas are obtained for the expected face numbers of sections of acute orthocentric simplices and crosspolytopes with uniformly distributed linear subspaces translated by a fixed vector. The translation vector is assumed to lie outside the affine hulls of all proper faces of the polytope. All solid angles entering these formulas are expressed as integrals of dimension at most two. This application includes regular simplices and regular crosspolytopes as special cases.

metadata.title: An $L^1$ bound for Ricci curvature on Kähler manifolds
metadata.abstract: We prove a uniform $L^1$ bound for Ricci curvature on noncollapsed Kähler manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below. metadata.title: Generalized quadratic matrix manifolds: Riemannian geometry and computations
metadata.abstract: We study the set $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$ of real $n\times p$ matrices $X$ satisfying $X^\top Q X = P$, where the nonsingular matrices $P$ and $Q$ are both symmetric or both skew-symmetric and the set is nonempty. Special choices of $P$ and $Q$ yield the Stiefel, generalized Stiefel, indefinite Stiefel, and symplectic Stiefel manifolds, as well as the quadratic matrix Lie groups. We prove that $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$ is a closed embedded submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$ and that it is compact exactly when $P$ and $Q$ are both symmetric and definite of the same sign. We derive closed-form expressions for its tangent space and, under a canonical-like Riemannian metric, for the normal space, the orthogonal projection, and the Riemannian gradient and Hessian. We extend the Cayley, quasi-geodesic, and polar retractions to $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$, with explicit domains, vector transports, and closed-form second-order corrections. These objects are the ingredients of Riemannian first- and second-order methods. In trace minimization tests with symmetric positive-definite, skew-symmetric, and symmetric indefinite pairs $(P,Q)$, the Riemannian conjugate gradient and trust-region methods reach the same objective value with different retractions and keep the iterates on $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$ up to rounding error.

metadata.title: The Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation on Riemannian manifolds
metadata.abstract: We establish geometric and analytic rigidity results for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation. On a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the existence of a positive critical point of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg quotient forces the manifold to be Euclidean and the solution to be extremal. No minimizing assumption or volume growth hypothesis is required, thereby strengthening earlier rigidity results. In Euclidean space, we prove that all positive solutions of the normalized equation whose nonlinear mass on expanding annuli has sublinear growth are extremals. The linear threshold is optimal, as shown by explicit profiles that are constant in one direction. We also prove a sharp pointwise estimate involving the solution and its gradient, valid without assumptions at infinity, with equality at one point characterizing the extremals. The proofs use weighted divergence identities and a reflection argument controlled by annular mass. Explicit constructions reveal the geometric and variational limits of rigidity: nonflat quotient critical points exist beyond the curvature hypothesis, while the normalized equation admits positive solutions even under strictly positive sectional curvature and maximal volume growth.

metadata.title: Learning Normal Coordinates on Riemannian Manifolds with Flow Charts
metadata.abstract: Riemannian manifolds are powerful models for problems with non-Euclidean structure. Recent work in geometric machine learning has focused on training deep neural networks to learn Riemannian metrics from high-dimensional data. However, many geometric algorithms require repeated evaluations of the exponential and logarithmic maps, whose high computational cost restricts the utility of learned Riemannian manifolds in practice. We propose to address this cost by training a conditional invertible neural network, called a flow chart, to approximate normal coordinates around points on a given Riemannian manifold. With this approach, the exponential and logarithmic maps can be approximated by fast Euclidean operations in the model's learned coordinate space. Our main contribution is an efficient loss function for training flow charts that is nonnegative and, under suitable domain assumptions, is zero precisely when the chart is normal. Across sixteen synthetic and data-derived geometries, flow charts are competitive with a specialized neural geodesic interpolator for logarithmic map estimation, while also being able to estimate the exponential map. When pretrained, flow charts provide a median speedup of 60-70x over numerical baselines at comparable logarithmic map estimation error, and their learned coordinates improve the accuracy of a numerical geodesic solver.

analysisBasis.abstract: Riemannian manifolds are powerful models for problems with non-Euclidean structure. Recent work in geometric machine learning has focused on training deep neural networks to learn Riemannian metrics from high-dimensional data. However, many geometric algorithms require repeated evaluations of the exponential and logarithmic maps, whose high computational cost restricts the utility of learned Riemannian manifolds in practice. We propose to address this cost by training a conditional invertible neural network, called a flow chart, to approximate normal coordinates around points on a given Riemannian manifold. With this approach, the exponential and logarithmic maps can be approximated by fast Euclidean operations in the model's learned coordinate space. Our main contribution is an efficient loss function for training flow charts that is nonnegative and, under suitable domain assumptions, is zero precisely when the chart is normal. Across sixteen synthetic and data-derived geometries, flow charts are competitive with a specialized neural geodesic interpolator for logarithmic map estimation, while also being able to estimate the exponential map. When pretrained, flow charts provide a median speedup of 60-70x over numerical baselines at comparable logarithmic map estimation error, and their learned coordinates improve the accuracy of a numerical geodesic solver.

metadata.title: Area gaps for minimal surfaces in spheres
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we prove that a linearly full minimal $2$-torus in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 5$ must have area $>2\pi^2$, and that a linearly full closed minimal surface in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 9$ must have area $>8\pi$. These results verify the Willmore conjecture and the generalized Willmore conjecture in higher codimension for minimal surfaces. The area gaps are obtained by applying the Cheng--Li--Yau comparison theorem and deriving a lower bound of the heat trace, where the monotonicity of the shifted normalized Riesz mean is used. We also establish a volume gap above the balanced Clifford product for linearly full closed minimal $n$-submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^N$ when $n=3$, $N\geq 9$, or $n\geq 4$, $N\geq 3n-1$.

metadata.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
metadata.abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.

metadata.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
metadata.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Zúñiga, are given.

metadata.title: Hyperbolic comparison and rigidity for the hyperspherical radius
metadata.abstract: We prove Gromov's hyperbolic hyperspherical radius comparison and rigidity conjectures in all dimensions $n\ge3$, without the spin assumption. Let $(X^n, g)$ be a smooth, oriented, connected, compact Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth connected boundary $S$. If ${\rm Sc}_g\ge -n(n-1)$ and $H_S\ge (n-1)\coth R$ for some $R>0$, then ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)\le\sinh R$, with equality if and only if $(X^n,g)$ is isometric to the closed hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$. Under the same curvature bounds, every smooth $1$-Lipschitz map of nonzero degree from $S$ to the boundary of the hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$ extends to an isometry of the fillings. Here, $g_S$ is the induced boundary metric, $H_S$ is the mean curvature of $S$ with respect to the outward unit normal, and ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)$ denotes the hyperspherical radius.

metadata.title: On the Geometry of Low Rank Correlation Matrices
metadata.abstract: Correlation matrices of bounded rank form a stratified space whose factor representations lie in a product of spheres. Using the orbit-type description of the rank stratification, we prove that padding factors preserves the Riemannian geometry of each fixed-rank stratum and the intrinsic length metric of every rank-bounded subset. In the reduced model, a Sylvester equation describes the mechanical connection and its horizontal lifts. We derive sectional-curvature formulas and bounds, characterize zero-curvature directions, and determine the connection's holonomy groups. In particular, a flat rank-two connection can have nontrivial dihedral holonomy. For geodesics subject to a rank bound, rank cannot decrease in the interior of a minimizing segment with maximal-rank endpoints; the local excess over the unconstrained quotient distance is controlled by a dimension-independent cubic estimate. Finally, we compute the exact change of measure between quotient Riemannian volume and Euclidean surface volume in the off-diagonal entries. Coarea yields explicit factor densities for both normalized uniform laws.

metadata.title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
metadata.abstract: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.

metadata.title: The $λ>0$ case for $Δu=λ-c e^u$ type equation on high dimensional spheres
metadata.abstract: Motivated by prescribed Chern scalar curvature problems in complex geometry, we study the equation $\Delta_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}V+\lambda(e^V-1)=0$ with $\lambda>0$ on spheres. For $N\ge4$ and $\lambda>2(N-2)$ with $\lambda\ne2N$, we prove the existence of a nonconstant smooth solution that is axially symmetric and symmetric about the equator.

metadata.title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
metadata.abstract: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $\delta^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{\delta+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,\Delta}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $\Delta(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $\delta+1={\rm deg}\,\Delta$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.

metadata.title: Local crystallization in three-dimensional quantization
metadata.abstract: A long-standing conjecture on the quantization problem due to Gersho, which remains open in dimensions higher than two, posits that optimal quantizers crystallize into a lattice structure; in dimension three, the natural candidate is the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, known to be optimal among other lattices. In this paper, we establish the asymptotic local optimality of the BCC lattice under small periodic perturbations, extending its known stability beyond the class of lattice configurations. Our approach connects the discrete geometry of Voronoi tessellations with a continuum variational problem, showing that the rescaled quadratic quantization energies converge to a continuum functional describing locally deformed BCC lattices. A central ingredient is a geometric and algebraic framework that combines the stability of the BCC Voronoi structure, a discrete calculus on its adjacency graph and an analysis of the lattice symmetries via representation theory, allowing us to establish the positivity of the second variation at the BCC configuration and thereby prove the local minimality of the BCC lattice for the limiting energy.

metadata.title: Singular solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation II
metadata.abstract: Continuing our work in [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 1503-1518], we construct new singular solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation with constant right-hand side in the Bedford-Taylor sense. Let $\mathbb D$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb C$. For $n\geq 2$, these solutions include: (i) a bounded solution on $\mathbb D^n$ that is discontinuous almost everywhere and nowhere classically differentiable; (ii) a continuous exhaustion of $\mathbb C^n$ that does not belong to $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb C^n)$; (iii) a continuous solution on $\overline{\mathbb D^n}$ whose Laplacian has a singular part. We construct these solutions from singular harmonic functions using partial Legendre transforms and holomorphic pullbacks.
